chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The stoning is the greater Penalty of Allah, and the lashing is the lesser Penalty of Allah.

key_terms.حَدُّ اللَّهِ: The Penalty of Allah (divine fixed punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the greater and lesser divine penalties in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly categorizes stoning (al-rajm) as the 'greatest' divine penalty and lashing as the 'lesser,' establishing a clear jurisprudential hierarchy for hudud. This distinction is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining the gravity of offenses and the corresponding severity of retribution, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of applying these penalties. The terminology underscores the theological weight of each punishment as a direct manifestation of God's law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The stoning is the bigger Penalty (Hadd) of Allahazwj, and the lashing is the smaller Penalty (Hadd) of Allahazwj’.
